name: @athenode/cli

tools.name: specs_list
tools.description: List the project's specifications, optionally filtered by status (draft | prepared | processing | completed) and scoped to a parent (`parentId`, CLI --parent) or to the top level (`topLevel`, CLI --top-level); the two are mutually exclusive. To find specs by topic, use specs_tree with `query` instead of walking this list. Returns an array ({items} in structuredContent).

parentId.description: Only direct children of this id (CLI: --parent).

tools.name: specs_search
tools.description: Flat search over the project's specifications: matches only, without ancestors or filters. The query must not be empty. Each match's `snippet` holds the matched text when the server found the match by meaning, and is otherwise null or absent. Prefer specs_tree with `query` for matches nested with their ancestors. Returns an array ({items} in structuredContent).

tools.name: specs_tree
tools.description: Fetch specifications as a tree, in one of four modes. Default: the subtree rooted at `id`. `branch`: a single chain from the top-level ancestor down to `id`, which is the deepest node. `query`: ranked search matches (at most 20) nested with their ancestors in one call, so there is no need to walk specs_list; `id` optionally scopes matches to its direct children; a match's `snippet` holds the matched text when the server found the match by meaning, and is otherwise null or absent; if a query finds little, retry with other wording. `executionOrder`: the unfiltered subtree under `id` plus the order in which its leaves can be implemented and the blockers holding them back. Only prepared/processing leaves are planned; draft leaves count as unprepared blockers. A root without children is its own only candidate, so call it on a leaf to get that leaf's blockers. Leaves inherit blockers from their ancestors up to and including the root. A cycle yields an empty order instead of an error. The result is a consistent one-time snapshot. `status` (draft | prepared | processing | completed) prunes branches without a matching node. Mode rules (errors use CLI flags): --execution-order requires an id and cannot combine with --branch, --query or --status; --query and --branch are exclusive and the query must not be empty; --branch cannot combine with --status. Returns an array of nodes, or `{tree, plan}` with executionOrder.

id.description: Root specification id (optional only in query mode).

status.description: Keep nodes with this status or a matching descendant (CLI: --status).

tools.name: specs_get
tools.description: Get one specification by id, with its content, status, implementation plan and direct blockers.

tools.name: specs_create
tools.description: Create a specification (status draft | prepared | processing | completed; content inline). `blockedBy` lists specs that must be completed first; the spec and its blockers are created atomically. Adding is all-or-nothing. A blocker that is missing, in another project, the spec itself, already completed, or an ancestor or descendant is rejected with 400; a link that already exists or would create a cycle with 409, so remove wrong links before adding new ones. Children inherit their ancestors' blockers. `todoCardId` creates the spec from a ToDo card, linking the two in the same request.

todoCardId.description: Id of the ToDo card the specification is created from (CLI: --todo-card). The backend records the new specification as the card's resulting specification in the same request. A missing card or a card of another project is rejected with 400; a card that already has a resulting specification is a conflict (409, code `todo_card_already_linked`) and is never overwritten. The call fails with code `TODO_CARD_LINK_NOT_RECORDED`, returning the created specification, if the link turns out not to be recorded.

tools.name: specs_update
tools.description: Update a specification; only supplied fields change, and `null` clears `summary`, `content` or `parentId` (CLI: --clear-summary, --clear-content, --clear-parent). `blockedBy` adds to the existing blockers, never replacing them; it is a second request, and its failure reports in `patchApplied` whether the field update was saved. Adding is all-or-nothing. A blocker that is missing, in another project, the spec itself, already completed, or an ancestor or descendant is rejected with 400; a link that already exists or would create a cycle with 409, so remove wrong links before adding new ones. Children inherit their ancestors' blockers.

parentId.description: New parent id; null clears it (CLI: --parent / --clear-parent).

blockedBy.description: Ids to add as blockers (CLI: --blocked-by, repeatable).

tools.name: specs_delete
tools.description: Delete a specification and all its descendants, without confirmation. Refused, listing the dependents, while other specs are blocked by it or its descendants, unless `force` is true.

force.description: Delete even when other specs depend on it (CLI: --force).

tools.name: specs_set_status
tools.description: Set the status of a specification (draft | prepared | processing | completed).

tools.name: specs_set_plan
tools.description: Set the implementation plan of a specification; this overwrites any previous plan, and `plan: null` clears it (CLI: --plan / --clear-plan).

plan.description: Plan text, or null to clear it.

tools.name: specs_get_plan
tools.description: Get the implementation plan of a specification (null when none is set).

tools.name: specs_qa_list
tools.description: List the questions and answers of a specification; an unanswered question has a null `answer`. Returns an array ({items} in structuredContent).

tools.name: specs_qa_add
tools.description: Add a question to a specification. `question` is a single string, so put any answer options inside it as Markdown.

tools.name: specs_qa_answer
tools.description: Answer a question previously added to a specification.

tools.name: specs_blockers_list
tools.description: List the specifications `id` is directly blocked by (not those inherited from ancestors). Returns an array ({items} in structuredContent).

tools.name: specs_blockers_add
tools.description: Mark `id` as blocked by each of `blockerIds`, returning the updated blocker list. Adding is all-or-nothing. A blocker that is missing, in another project, the spec itself, already completed, or an ancestor or descendant is rejected with 400; a link that already exists or would create a cycle with 409, so remove wrong links before adding new ones. Children inherit their ancestors' blockers. Returns an array ({items} in structuredContent).

blockerIds.description: Ids of the specs that must be completed first.

tools.name: specs_blockers_remove
tools.description: Remove the direct link that blocks `id` by `blockerId`; 404 when no such link exists. Blockers inherited from an ancestor must be removed on that ancestor.

tools.name: todos_list
tools.description: List the project's ToDo cards. Without `status` only `open` cards are returned; closed cards (`done`, `dismissed`) only when asked for. `specificationId` keeps the cards whose origin or resulting specification is that one. Rows are full cards including `description` and `questions` (each card's open questions with their answers), ordered by priority, then newest. Returns an array ({items} in structuredContent).

status.description: Statuses to return (open | done | dismissed); omitted or empty means open (CLI: --status, repeatable).

specificationId.description: Only cards whose origin or resulting specification is this id (CLI: --specification).

tools.name: todos_get
tools.description: Get one ToDo card by id, with its `status`, its `resultingSpecificationId` (null until the card is converted into a specification) and its `questions`: the card's open questions, each with its `answer` (null while unanswered). A 403 can also mean that no such card exists.

tools.name: todos_create
tools.description: Create a ToDo card. Every card starts `open` (a project token creates it with source `agent`), so there is no status parameter. `type` defaults to `idea` and `priority` to `medium`. `questions` gives the card up to 3 open questions, and only when a decision that only the user can make blocks the card; this is the only way for an agent to add a question, since there is no tool to add one to an existing card. The Free plan's card limit is reported as a plan-limit error.

type.description: Card type (follow-up | tech-debt | bug | idea); default idea.

priority.description: Card priority (low | medium | high); default medium.

originSpecificationId.description: Specification whose work the card came out of (CLI: --origin-specification).

questions.description: Open questions of the card, at most 3; each is one string, Markdown, with its answer options inside the text (CLI: --question, repeatable). A card's open questions are decisions to make before it is carried out. Add one only when the card cannot be carried out without a decision that only the user can make: a product choice, mutually exclusive approaches with a real trade-off, or an irreversible or destructive action. Never ask what can be found in the code, the conventions or the settings, and never ask "just in case"; most cards have none. Give a question its answer options, in the project's question format (recommended option first and marked), when they can be enumerated.

tools.name: todos_set_status
tools.description: Set the status of a ToDo card (open | done | dismissed). A project token may only close an `open` card, as `done` (carried out, with or without a resulting specification) or `dismissed` (closed without being carried out); reopening a card and moving it between `done` and `dismissed` are refused with 403. Repeating the closed status a card already has succeeds unchanged. A 403 can also mean that no such card exists.

status.description: New status; a project token may only set done or dismissed, on an open card.

tools.name: todos_qa_answer
tools.description: Record the answer to one unanswered open question of a ToDo card; the question ids come with the card (`questions` of `todos_get` and `todos_list`). A project token cannot change an existing answer: answering a question that already has one is refused with 403. A question id that does not belong to the card is a 404. A 403 can also mean that no such card exists.

tools.name: setups_files_list
tools.description: List the files and directories directly inside a directory of the installed setup's file tree (the project's own setup copy), or the root without `path`. `setupId` targets another setup of the project instead of the installed one. Returns an array ({items} in structuredContent).

path.description: Directory path, e.g. "settings"; root if omitted.

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

tools.name: setups_files_get
tools.description: Get one file of the installed setup's file tree by path, with its content and summary. Workflow settings are read this way, e.g. "settings/SETTINGS.md". `setupId` targets another setup of the project instead of the installed one.

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

tools.name: setups_files_create
tools.description: Create a file, or a directory with `dir: true`, in the installed setup's file tree, creating missing parents. File content is inline, at most 50000 characters; directories have no content. `setupId` targets another setup of the project instead of the installed one.

path.description: Path of the new file or directory.

dir.description: Create a directory instead of a file (CLI: --dir).

summary.description: Short summary of the file or directory.

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

tools.name: setups_files_update
tools.description: Replace a file's content and/or summary; only given fields change. Content is inline, at most 50000 characters. Directories cannot be updated. `setupId` targets another setup of the project instead of the installed one.

summary.description: The new summary; null or "" clears it.

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

tools.name: setups_files_delete
tools.description: Delete a file or empty directory, without confirmation; a non-empty directory needs `recursive: true` and is deleted with everything under it. `setupId` targets another setup of the project instead of the installed one.

path.description: Path of the file or directory.

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

tools.name: setups_clone
tools.description: Clone an agent setup under a new name in the project, keeping its description. The whole setup is copied: agents and skills as independent copies, rules, files and the MCP servers with their stored `env`/`headers` values. It counts against the plan limits (setups, and agents, skills and MCP servers per setup); a breach creates nothing. `source` is a setup name, or an id with `byId: true`. The installed setup is not changed.

source.description: Name (or, with byId, id) of the setup to clone.

name.description: The new cloned setup's name, at most 200 characters.

byId.description: The given value is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --by-id <id>).

tools.name: setups_create
tools.description: Create an empty agent setup in the project. Without `slug` the server derives one from the name. A `slug` is refused, writing nothing, with code `setup_slug_conflict` (409: another setup of the project has it), `setup_slug_forbidden` (a reserved slug), `setup_slug_locked` (the slug of this setup cannot be changed) or `setup_slug_invalid` (not a valid slug).

name.description: The new setup's name, at most 200 characters.

description.description: The new setup's description, at most 25000 characters.

slug.description: The new setup's slug (CLI: --slug). Unique in the project; it is the name of the setup's plugin and the prefix of its commands.

tools.name: setups_list
tools.description: List all agent setups in the project, each with its `slug` (unique in the project: the name of the setup's plugin and the prefix of its commands). A setup added from the setup library has a `libraryOrigin` (`null` otherwise) naming its origin entry, its `version`, the entry's `latestVersion` and whether an update is on offer (`updateAvailable`; see library_update_preview). Returns an array ({items} in structuredContent).

tools.name: setups_update
tools.description: Change an agent setup's name, description and/or slug (at least one); omitted fields keep their value. `target` is a setup name, or an id with `byId: true`, never a slug. A changed slug renames the setup's plugin and its commands: the result then has a warning naming the old and the new slug. It does not regenerate the install, even for the installed setup: the local install follows at the next `athenode init` or regeneration. A `slug` is refused, writing nothing, with code `setup_slug_conflict` (409: another setup of the project has it), `setup_slug_forbidden` (a reserved slug), `setup_slug_locked` (the slug of this setup cannot be changed) or `setup_slug_invalid` (not a valid slug).

target.description: Name (or, with byId, id) of the setup to update.

name.description: The setup's new name, at most 200 characters.

description.description: The setup's new description, at most 25000 characters.

slug.description: The setup's new slug (CLI: --slug); the current one is kept if omitted. Unique in the project; it is the name of the setup's plugin and the prefix of its commands.

byId.description: The given value is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --by-id <id>).

tools.name: setups_pull_preview
tools.description: Preview pulling another setup of the project into a setup, changing nothing: per kind (skills, agents, MCP servers, files) the items it would `add`, those in `conflict` with the setup (and whether they are `replaceable`) and the `identical` ones, the state of the rules, and the `sourceFingerprint` and `fingerprint` that setups_pull needs with decisions. The source is read as it is now; an item's `libraryItemId` is the id of the source setup's item. `source` is the setup the content is taken from and `setup` the one that receives it: each is the setup's exact, case-sensitive name, or its id with `sourceById: true` / `setupById: true` (see setups_list). Both are required, both are setups of the project and they must differ; the installed setup is never assumed. A setup of another project cannot be the source (pulling across projects exists only in the web app); for a library entry use library_merge.

source.description: Name of the setup to pull from, or its id with sourceById. Required.

sourceById.description: `source` is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --source-by-id).

setup.description: Name of the setup that receives the content, or its id with setupById (CLI: --setup). Required.

setupById.description: `setup` is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --setup-by-id).

tools.name: setups_pull
tools.description: Pull another setup of the project into a setup, in one transaction, and return what was added and replaced per kind. It is a one-time copy: skills and agents become new, independent items of the setup, nothing is ever deleted from it, nothing about the source is recorded and no update is offered later. Without `decisions` (safe mode) it previews and applies in one call: every new item is added, nothing is replaced and the rules are kept. `decisions` is an object in the preview's shape: `sourceFingerprint` and `fingerprint` from the preview, and per kind (`skills`, `agents`, `mcpServers`, `files`) the lists `add` and `replace` of `{name}` items (`{path}` for files). A kind without an `add` list adds everything new; a present `add` list, even an empty one, adds exactly its items. `replace` overwrites conflicting items of the setup and needs `confirmReplace: true`. `rules` is `keep` (default), `append` (under a heading with the source setup's name) or `replace`. A whole preview may be passed back as `decisions`: it adds every new item and replaces nothing. A `library_merge_stale` error means `setup` or `source` changed since the preview: repeat setups_pull_preview and apply with its values. A refusal writes nothing. `source` is the setup the content is taken from and `setup` the one that receives it: each is the setup's exact, case-sensitive name, or its id with `sourceById: true` / `setupById: true` (see setups_list). Both are required, both are setups of the project and they must differ; the installed setup is never assumed. A setup of another project cannot be the source (pulling across projects exists only in the web app); for a library entry use library_merge. When `setup` is the installed setup, it is then regenerated locally, like `athenode init` without confirmation (the result adds `install` and `regeneration`); if that fails, the backend change is still saved and the tool returns an error. Any other setup is changed on the server only.

source.description: Name of the setup to pull from, or its id with sourceById. Required.

sourceById.description: `source` is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --source-by-id).

setup.description: Name of the setup that receives the content, or its id with setupById (CLI: --setup). Required.

setupById.description: `setup` is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --setup-by-id).

decisions.description: Decisions in the preview's shape: {sourceFingerprint, fingerprint, confirmReplace?, skills?, agents?, mcpServers?, files?, rules?}, each kind as {add?: [...], replace?: [...]} and rules one of keep | append | replace (CLI: --decisions). Safe mode if omitted.

tools.name: setups_delete
tools.description: Delete an agent setup immediately, without confirmation. `target` is a setup name, or an id with `byId: true`. Deleting the installed setup adds a warning.

target.description: Name (or, with byId, id) of the setup to delete.

byId.description: The given value is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --by-id <id>).

tools.name: agents_create
tools.description: Create an agent and attach it to the installed setup. `prompt` is the inline prompt/instructions; `description` is usually required metadata, and missing required metadata fails instead of prompting. Then regenerates the installed setup locally, like `athenode init` without confirmation (the result adds `install` and `regeneration`, whose `pluginChanges` lists the tools whose plugin package or declaration was rewritten, with `suppressedIn` naming another tool's local settings file the plugin was switched off in; `missingEnvVars` is checked against the MCP server's environment, not your shell). If regeneration fails, the backend change is still saved and the tool returns an error. Requires an installed setup (`npx @athenode/cli init`), unless `setupId` names another setup of the project: that one is changed on the server only, with no local regeneration.

metadata.description: Metadata fields to set, as {key: value}; "<target>.<field>" sets a per-target field (target: claudecode, codexcli, cursor, copilot, copilotcli, opencode, antigravity-ide, antigravity-cli, devin, junie, kiro-ide, kiro-cli, kilo, factorydroid, grokcli, qoder, commandcode, codewhale, mimocode, zcode, vibe, rovodev, zoocode, pool, qwencode, codebuddy, augmentcode, goose, kimi-code, deepagents, omp, reasonix, bob). Booleans and numbers may be JSON values or strings; list fields an array or a comma-separated string. Unlisted metadata is kept on update.

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

tools.name: agents_update
tools.description: Fork-update an agent of the installed setup (by name, or id with `byId`): a new backend row gets the changes, keeping unchanged fields and metadata, and replaces the old row in the setup in the same request; the server deletes the old row unless another setup still links it. A `rename` to the name of another one in the setup is refused (409, code `agent_name_conflict`) and changes nothing. Then regenerates the installed setup locally, like `athenode init` without confirmation (the result adds `install` and `regeneration`, whose `pluginChanges` lists the tools whose plugin package or declaration was rewritten, with `suppressedIn` naming another tool's local settings file the plugin was switched off in; `missingEnvVars` is checked against the MCP server's environment, not your shell). If regeneration fails, the backend change is still saved and the tool returns an error. Requires an installed setup (`npx @athenode/cli init`), unless `setupId` names another setup of the project: that one is changed on the server only, with no local regeneration.

identifier.description: Agent name, or its backend id with byId.

byId.description: `identifier` is a backend id, not a name (CLI: --by-id).

rename.description: New name; the current one is kept if omitted.

metadata.description: Metadata fields to set, as {key: value}; "<target>.<field>" sets a per-target field (target: claudecode, codexcli, cursor, copilot, copilotcli, opencode, antigravity-ide, antigravity-cli, devin, junie, kiro-ide, kiro-cli, kilo, factorydroid, grokcli, qoder, commandcode, codewhale, mimocode, zcode, vibe, rovodev, zoocode, pool, qwencode, codebuddy, augmentcode, goose, kimi-code, deepagents, omp, reasonix, bob). Booleans and numbers may be JSON values or strings; list fields an array or a comma-separated string. Unlisted metadata is kept on update.

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

tools.name: agents_remove
tools.description: Detach an agent (by name, or id with `byId`) from the installed setup without confirmation, removing its generated files; the server deletes the row itself once no setup links it any more (one another setup still links is kept). Then regenerates the installed setup locally, like `athenode init` without confirmation (the result adds `install` and `regeneration`, whose `pluginChanges` lists the tools whose plugin package or declaration was rewritten, with `suppressedIn` naming another tool's local settings file the plugin was switched off in; `missingEnvVars` is checked against the MCP server's environment, not your shell). If regeneration fails, the backend change is still saved and the tool returns an error. Requires an installed setup (`npx @athenode/cli init`), unless `setupId` names another setup of the project: that one is changed on the server only, with no local regeneration.

identifier.description: Agent name, or its backend id with byId.

byId.description: `identifier` is a backend id, not a name (CLI: --by-id).

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

tools.name: mcp_servers_create
tools.description: Create a setup-level MCP server on the installed setup: `command`, `args` and `env` for "stdio", `url` and `headers` for "http"/"sse" (the other transport's fields are ignored). Values may reference environment variables as ${VAR}. Then regenerates the installed setup locally, like `athenode init` without confirmation (the result adds `install` and `regeneration`, whose `pluginChanges` lists the tools whose plugin package or declaration was rewritten, with `suppressedIn` naming another tool's local settings file the plugin was switched off in; `missingEnvVars` is checked against the MCP server's environment, not your shell). If regeneration fails, the backend change is still saved and the tool returns an error. Requires an installed setup (`npx @athenode/cli init`), unless `setupId` names another setup of the project: that one is changed on the server only, with no local regeneration.

args.description: Arguments of the command (stdio; CLI: --arg, repeatable).

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

tools.name: mcp_servers_update
tools.description: Update a setup-level MCP server (by name, or id with `byId`) in place. Omitted fields keep their value; a given `args`, `env` or `headers` replaces the whole value, so include every entry to keep. Switching the transport drops the old transport's fields. Then regenerates the installed setup locally, like `athenode init` without confirmation (the result adds `install` and `regeneration`, whose `pluginChanges` lists the tools whose plugin package or declaration was rewritten, with `suppressedIn` naming another tool's local settings file the plugin was switched off in; `missingEnvVars` is checked against the MCP server's environment, not your shell). If regeneration fails, the backend change is still saved and the tool returns an error. Requires an installed setup (`npx @athenode/cli init`), unless `setupId` names another setup of the project: that one is changed on the server only, with no local regeneration.

identifier.description: MCP server name, or its backend id with byId.

byId.description: `identifier` is a backend id, not a name (CLI: --by-id).

args.description: New arguments (stdio); replaces the current list.

env.description: New environment variables (stdio); replaces the current map.

headers.description: New HTTP headers (http/sse); replaces the current map.

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

If regeneration fails, the backend change is still saved and the tool returns an error. Requires an installed setup (`npx @athenode/cli init`), unless `setupId` names another setup of the project: that one is changed on the server only, with no local regeneration.

identifier.description: MCP server name, or its backend id with byId.

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

tools.name: rules_update

The content is literal (a leading "@" is not a file reference); over 50000 characters it adds a warning and may be rejected. Then regenerates the installed setup locally, like `athenode init` without confirmation (the result adds `install` and `regeneration`, whose `pluginChanges` lists the tools whose plugin package or declaration was rewritten, with `suppressedIn` naming another tool's local settings file the plugin was switched off in; `missingEnvVars` is checked against the MCP server's environment, not your shell). If regeneration fails, the backend change is still saved and the tool returns an error. Requires an installed setup (`npx @athenode/cli init`), unless `setupId` names another setup of the project: that one is changed on the server only, with no local regeneration.

setupId.description: Id of the agent setup to act on (see setups_list); the installed setup if omitted.

tools.name: library_list
tools.description: List or search the public setup library, one page at a time, most liked first. Returns `{items, nextCursor}` with no total; for the next page pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` with the same `query` and `tag` (a cursor is invalid with other values). Readable with any project token.

cursor.description: The nextCursor of the previous page.

tools.name: library_get
tools.description: Get one library entry: its metadata, versions and the agents, skills (with their bundle files as `{path, isText}`; `isText: false` is a binary file), MCP servers and files of its latest version, without their texts (read those with library_item). Item ids change with every published version. `entry` is the entry's exact name (matched case-insensitively, surrounding spaces ignored), or its id with `byId: true`; a value that looks like an id is still taken as a name without `byId`.

entry.description: Library entry name, or its id with byId.

byId.description: `entry` is an entry id, not a name (CLI: --by-id).

tools.name: library_item
tools.description: Read the content of one item of a library entry's latest version. `agent`, `skill` and `mcp-server` need `itemId` (from library_get, or a merge preview's `libraryItemId`); `file` needs `path`; `skill-file` needs `itemId` (the skill) and `path`, returns `{path, content}` and refuses a binary file; `rules` needs neither. Any other combination is refused. Items are not addressed by name: names are not unique inside an entry. `entry` is the entry's exact name (matched case-insensitively, surrounding spaces ignored), or its id with `byId: true`; a value that looks like an id is still taken as a name without `byId`.

entry.description: Library entry name, or its id with byId.

byId.description: `entry` is an entry id, not a name (CLI: --by-id).

path.description: Path of the setup file, or of the file inside the skill.

tools.name: library_add
tools.description: Add a library entry to the project as a new setup, a full copy of its latest version, and return the setup. The server only is changed: no local file is written and nothing is installed (run `npx @athenode/cli init --setup <id or slug>` to install it, both of which are in the result). A name the project already uses is refused with code `setup_name_conflict` and a free `suggestedName`. `entry` is the entry's exact name (matched case-insensitively, surrounding spaces ignored), or its id with `byId: true`; a value that looks like an id is still taken as a name without `byId`.

entry.description: Library entry name, or its id with byId.

byId.description: `entry` is an entry id, not a name (CLI: --by-id).

name.description: The new setup's name, at most 200 characters; the entry's name if omitted.

tools.name: library_merge_preview
tools.description: Preview merging a library entry's latest version into a setup, changing nothing: per kind the items it would `add`, those in `conflict` with the setup (and whether they are `replaceable`) and the `identical` ones, the state of the rules, and the `entryVersion` and `fingerprint` that library_merge needs with decisions. Compare both sides of a conflict with library_item and the setup's own tools. `entry` is the entry's exact name (matched case-insensitively, surrounding spaces ignored), or its id with `byId: true`; a value that looks like an id is still taken as a name without `byId`. `setup` is required and is the setup's exact, case-sensitive name, or its id with `setupById: true` (see setups_list); the installed setup is never assumed.

entry.description: Library entry name, or its id with byId.

byId.description: `entry` is an entry id, not a name (CLI: --by-id).

setup.description: Name of the setup to act on, or its id with setupById (CLI: --setup). Required.

setupById.description: `setup` is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --setup-by-id).

tools.name: library_merge
tools.description: Merge a library entry's latest version into a setup, in one transaction, and return what was added and replaced per kind. Without `decisions` (safe mode) it previews and applies in one call: every new item is added, nothing is replaced and the rules are kept. `decisions` is an object in the preview's shape: `entryVersion` and `fingerprint` from the preview, and per kind (`skills`, `agents`, `mcpServers`, `files`) the lists `add` and `replace` of `{name}` items (`{path}` for files). A kind without an `add` list adds everything new; a present `add` list, even an empty one, adds exactly its items. `replace` overwrites conflicting items of the setup and needs `confirmReplace: true`. `rules` is `keep` (default), `append` or `replace`. A whole preview may be passed back as `decisions`: it adds every new item and replaces nothing. A `library_merge_stale` error means the setup or the entry changed since the preview: repeat the preview and apply with its values. A refusal writes nothing. `decisions.entryId`, when present, must be this entry. `entry` is the entry's exact name (matched case-insensitively, surrounding spaces ignored), or its id with `byId: true`; a value that looks like an id is still taken as a name without `byId`. `setup` is required and is the setup's exact, case-sensitive name, or its id with `setupById: true` (see setups_list); the installed setup is never assumed. When `setup` is the installed setup, it is then regenerated locally, like `athenode init` without confirmation (the result adds `install` and `regeneration`); if that fails, the backend change is still saved and the tool returns an error. Any other setup is changed on the server only.

entry.description: Library entry name, or its id with byId.

byId.description: `entry` is an entry id, not a name (CLI: --by-id).

setup.description: Name of the setup to act on, or its id with setupById (CLI: --setup). Required.

setupById.description: `setup` is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --setup-by-id).

decisions.description: Decisions in the preview's shape: {entryVersion, fingerprint, confirmReplace?, skills?, agents?, mcpServers?, files?, rules?}, each kind as {add?: [...], replace?: [...]} and rules one of keep | append | replace (CLI: --decisions). Safe mode if omitted.

tools.name: library_update_preview
tools.description: Preview updating a setup that was added from the library to the latest version of its origin entry, changing nothing: the same result as library_merge_preview for that entry. Refused with code `library_update_no_origin` for a setup that has no origin entry and `library_update_not_available` for one already at the latest version (setups_list shows `libraryOrigin.updateAvailable`). `setup` is required and is the setup's exact, case-sensitive name, or its id with `setupById: true` (see setups_list); the installed setup is never assumed.

setup.description: Name of the setup to act on, or its id with setupById (CLI: --setup). Required.

setupById.description: `setup` is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --setup-by-id).

tools.name: library_update
tools.description: Update a setup that was added from the library to the latest version of its origin entry, in one transaction, and return what was added and replaced per kind; the setup is then recorded at that version. Without `decisions` (safe mode) it previews and applies in one call: every new item is added, nothing is replaced and the rules are kept. `decisions` is an object in the preview's shape: `entryVersion` and `fingerprint` from the preview, and per kind (`skills`, `agents`, `mcpServers`, `files`) the lists `add` and `replace` of `{name}` items (`{path}` for files). A kind without an `add` list adds everything new; a present `add` list, even an empty one, adds exactly its items. `replace` overwrites conflicting items of the setup and needs `confirmReplace: true`. `rules` is `keep` (default), `append` or `replace`. A whole preview may be passed back as `decisions`: it adds every new item and replaces nothing. A `library_merge_stale` error means the setup or the entry changed since the preview: repeat the preview and apply with its values. A refusal writes nothing. Take the decisions' values from library_update_preview. `setup` is required and is the setup's exact, case-sensitive name, or its id with `setupById: true` (see setups_list); the installed setup is never assumed. When `setup` is the installed setup, it is then regenerated locally, like `athenode init` without confirmation (the result adds `install` and `regeneration`); if that fails, the backend change is still saved and the tool returns an error. Any other setup is changed on the server only.

setup.description: Name of the setup to act on, or its id with setupById (CLI: --setup). Required.

setupById.description: `setup` is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --setup-by-id).

decisions.description: Decisions in the preview's shape: {entryVersion, fingerprint, confirmReplace?, skills?, agents?, mcpServers?, files?, rules?}, each kind as {add?: [...], replace?: [...]} and rules one of keep | append | replace (CLI: --decisions). Safe mode if omitted.

tools.name: library_publish
tools.description: Publish a setup to the setup library: a new entry, or a new version of the entry the setup already has. Publishing makes the setup's agents, skills, MCP servers, files and rules visible to every signed-in Athenode user and turns the entry's public display on, unless an administrator made public display unavailable for the entry. Public display shows the entry's name, description and tags and the full content of its agents, skills with their bundle files, rules and setup files on the open web, without an account, where search engines can index them; MCP server configuration is not shown. After it is turned off, the entry can stay on the public site for up to a day and longer in search engines' caches. So publishing needs the explicit `confirmPublic: true`, the one consent to both; ask the user before setting it, naming the open web, and there is no `publicDisplay` here (to turn public display off afterwards use library_edit). Without `confirmPublic: true` nothing is published: the result is `{published: false, preview, problem}` with a warning, and a second one when an administrator excluded the entry from the public site (`publicDisplayBanned: true`: it is then published to the in-app library only; tell the user before confirming); the preview lists the items as `{id, name}` / `{id, path}` objects, and `problem` (`{status, code, field, error}`, else `null`) is the first refusal the publish would get: an invalid name, description, note or tags, or a name another entry has (`library_entry_name_taken`), which a confirmed publish answers as an error. The entry and the preview carry `publicDisplay` and `publicDisplayBanned` as stored, `null` in the preview of a setup with no entry yet. Refused in both modes: a plan that cannot publish and MCP servers holding literal `env`/`headers` values (code `mcp_literal_secrets`, with the `servers` and keys to turn into `${VAR}` references). Nothing is regenerated locally. `setup` is required and is the setup's exact, case-sensitive name, or its id with `setupById: true` (see setups_list); the installed setup is never assumed.

setup.description: Name of the setup to act on, or its id with setupById (CLI: --setup). Required.

setupById.description: `setup` is a setup id, not a name (CLI: --setup-by-id).

name.description: The entry's name; the setup's name (or the entry's current one) if omitted.

note.description: A note for the published version.

confirmPublic.description: Confirms what becomes visible, public display included (CLI: --confirm-public). Required to publish. Publishing makes the setup's agents, skills, MCP servers, files and rules visible to every signed-in Athenode user and turns the entry's public display on, unless an administrator made public display unavailable for the entry. Public display shows the entry's name, description and tags and the full content of its agents, skills with their bundle files, rules and setup files on the open web, without an account, where search engines can index them; MCP server configuration is not shown. After it is turned off, the entry can stay on the public site for up to a day and longer in search engines' caches.

tools.name: library_edit
tools.description: Change a library entry's name, description, tags and/or public display (at least one); omitted fields keep their value and no version is created. `description: ""` clears the description and `tags: []` clears the tags; given tags replace the current ones. Public display shows the entry's name, description and tags and the full content of its agents, skills with their bundle files, rules and setup files on the open web, without an account, where search engines can index them; MCP server configuration is not shown. After it is turned off, the entry can stay on the public site for up to a day and longer in search engines' caches. So `publicDisplay: true` needs `confirmPublic: true`, even when the entry already has it on, and is refused without it before anything is sent; ask the user specifically about public display before setting it. `publicDisplay: false` needs no confirmation. Turning it on for an entry an administrator excluded from the public site is refused with code `library_public_display_banned`. Allowed for those who may manage the entry. `entry` is the entry's exact name (matched case-insensitively, surrounding spaces ignored), or its id with `byId: true`; a value that looks like an id is still taken as a name without `byId`.

entry.description: Library entry name, or its id with byId.

byId.description: `entry` is an entry id, not a name (CLI: --by-id).

tags.description: The new tags, replacing the current ones; [] clears them (CLI: --tag, --clear-tags).

publicDisplay.description: Turns public display on (`true`, which needs `confirmPublic: true`) or off (`false`); omitted, the entry keeps its setting. Unlike `confirmPublic: false`, which equals an omitted one, `false` is a change (CLI: --public-display / --no-public-display).

confirmPublic.description: Confirms turning public display on (CLI: --confirm-public); required with `publicDisplay: true`, no change by itself. Publishing makes the setup's agents, skills, MCP servers, files and rules visible to every signed-in Athenode user and turns the entry's public display on, unless an administrator made public display unavailable for the entry. Public display shows the entry's name, description and tags and the full content of its agents, skills with their bundle files, rules and setup files on the open web, without an account, where search engines can index them; MCP server configuration is not shown. After it is turned off, the entry can stay on the public site for up to a day and longer in search engines' caches.

tools.name: library_unpublish
tools.description: Unpublish a library entry immediately, without confirmation: the entry and all its versions are removed from the library. Setups already added from it are kept. Allowed for those who may manage the entry. `entry` is the entry's exact name (matched case-insensitively, surrounding spaces ignored), or its id with `byId: true`; a value that looks like an id is still taken as a name without `byId`.

entry.description: Library entry name, or its id with byId.

byId.description: `entry` is an entry id, not a name (CLI: --by-id).

instructions:
Athenode: product specifications stored as a tree, plus the agent setup (agents, skills, rules, MCP servers, settings files) installed into this project.

The library_* tools work with the setup library, the agent setups published by Athenode projects: browse it, add an entry as a new setup, merge one into a setup, update a setup added from it, and publish a setup. Those that act on an existing setup take it as the required `setup`, never assuming the installed one. Publishing shows a setup to every signed-in Athenode user and turns its public display on, which puts its content on the open web: ask the user before confirming it (`confirmPublic`). library_unpublish removes an entry at once, without confirmation.

Every tool acts on the project root, the directory holding .athenode/config.json: the --project-dir option of `athenode mcp`, else the ATHENODE_PROJECT_DIR environment variable, else the server's working directory when it holds a config, else (when the client supports MCP roots) the first file:// root holding one. ATHENODE_TOKEN overrides the stored project token.

Initializing a project is CLI-only: run `npx @athenode/cli init` in the project root. Tools fail with code NOT_INITIALIZED until it has run.

Tools are named <group>_<subcommand> after the CLI command path, with dashes as underscores (e.g. `athenode specs qa add` is specs_qa_add, `athenode mcp-servers create` is mcp_servers_create); Claude Code shows them as mcp__athenode__<tool>. Results are the CLI's JSON output; errors are isError results with the CLI's error JSON plus `code`, `type` and `exitCode`.
